text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.

- The United Nations is very pleased with a human and minority rights package Croatia has offered to Serbs in the rebel enclave of Eastern Slavonia. There are now no obstacles to holding local elections there in March.

- Croatia is keen to open communications, transport and trade with southeastern Europe and...is ready to take its part of the responsibility for conditions in the neighbouring Balkans, Croatian president Franjo Tudjman said after meeting U.S. envoy John Kornblum.

- American Southeast European Cooperation Initiative (SECI) is totally unacceptable for Croatia as it wants to turn the region into some kind of obsolete Balkan America. Such a multi-cultural 'goulash' has never existed in Europe since nation-states were formed.
- Bosnian president Alija Izetbegovic has not given up the idea of forming the Islamic Bosnia and Herzegovina, says Bosnian Federation president Kresimir Zubak.
- This year will be a turning point for Nama, says the department store chain director Marija Sola. Nama expects some profit after renovating two of its key stores in Zagreb.
- Plastic factory Vinilplastika agrees to supply 100-300 tonnes of granules for plastic packaging to Turkish firm Gunesyat. The deal put at 8.0 million German marks a year.
- Average monthly salaries in public sector will rise by 26 percent to 2,650 kuna by the end of the year, analysts say. The rise for the goods and services sector is put at 16 percent to 2,400 kuna.
- Eurokuna bonds to be listed on the Zagreb Stock Exchange today.
- U.N. war crimes tribunal in The Hague improves prison conditions for Bosnian Croat general Tihomir Blaskic.
- Sibenik's textile firm Revija teeters on the brink of insolvency but might strike a deal with German clothes retailer Marc Aurel, says director Miljenko Stosic. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
